summary.headline: Uniparts Q2 FY27 revenue rose 37% YoY to ₹379 crore with 23.4% EBITDA margin, comfortably above its 20% through-cycle target.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was ₹379 crore, up 37% YoY and broadly in line with prior guidance; H1 revenue reached ₹726 crore, up 32%. Margin was 23.4% for Q2, and PAT rose 37% YoY to ₹54 crore in the quarter (H1 PAT ₹111 crore). Construction equipment sales grew 49% YoY, offsetting weakness in farm (agriculture) demand, where tractor volumes above 100 HP and 4WD were down about 17%. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth of about 24% over FY26 and expects Q3 to be seasonally weaker than Q2 and Q1.

financial_highlights.change: after ₹41 crore dividend paid in Q2

segments.name: Construction equipment
segments.commentary: Sales grew 49% YoY, driven by US data-centre/AI and smart-manufacturing demand and recovery in Europe. Management says the segment is the largest growth driver and 70% of new business awards are in construction or large ag.

segments.name: Small agriculture
segments.commentary: Sales grew 25% YoY; management sees green shoots of recovery in India and rest of world, though it expects India growth to slow in H2.

segments.name: Large agriculture (3-point linkage, >100 HP and 4WD tractors)
segments.commentary: Industry volumes down about 17%; management says Uniparts has returned to YoY growth here on new business wins. About 35% of new business awards are in large ag.

segments.name: Fabrication (third platform)
segments.commentary: Roughly 12-15% of new business wins; management expects it to be a meaningful contributor in 18-24 months and targets high single-digit percentage of revenue. Currently under 2% of revenue per analyst question, not disputed by management.

segments.name: Warehousing (delivery channel)
segments.commentary: Management called it the highest-margin channel; it was 53% of sales in Q2 versus 56% in Q1.

segments.name: Mexico facility
segments.commentary: First customer dispatches began in November 2026; expects single-digit USD million revenue in the next six months and is working with three customers.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue expected about 24% higher than FY26, with H2 FY27 growth of about 10%.
Q3 FY27 expected to be seasonally weaker, but above Q1 levels.
Through-cycle EBITDA margin target of at least 20% reiterated; H1 FY27 at 23.4% in Q2.
Capex of about ₹60 crore planned over the next year, mostly approved with advances paid; capex about 4% of revenue.
Working capital expected to stay around 136-140 days.
Trailing 12-month new business wins of ₹225 crore, each win ramping to peak over 2-3 years.
Acquisition pipeline of about half a dozen opportunities; first use of cash is acquisitions, with dividends as alternative if no deal.
capex_capacity: Q2 FY27 capex about ₹10 crore, focused on capability enhancement, productivity and customer-led growth.
About ₹60 crore capex planned over the next year, mostly approved with advances paid.
Mexico facility began first customer dispatches in November 2026, single-digit USD million revenue expected in next six months.
Fabrication capability expansion underway at the existing facility in India.
demand_pricing: Construction equipment recovery started in Q1 CY26 (or Q4 CY25) and management sees a multi-year cycle with visibility into multi-year data-centre-linked contracts.
Management reports no slowdown in order books after US midterm elections and no expected cancellations.
Material costs have been steady at 34-37% of revenue; Q2 at 34.3%. Some steel price increases not yet passed through, expected to flow in later.
Freight cost increase drove higher other expenses in Q2; management says it will be passed to customers and should recover next quarter.
Management reports no impact from FTC/USDA inquiry into US agricultural equipment companies.
Gross margin typically 63-66%; delivery-channel mix (warehousing highest margin, direct export/local lowest) is the main driver.

qa_highlights.question: How is the European demand environment, given the Russia-Ukraine war and energy prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a detailed Europe demand read in the transcript; it noted Europe growth in construction is driven by infrastructure and energy-transition investment and non-commercial construction taking off.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving gross margin resilience despite steel inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Material cost was 34.3% in Q2, within the 34-37% range; some steel inflation is not yet passed to customers and will come through later. Delivery-channel mix is the larger margin driver than product mix.

qa_highlights.question: Is the construction growth structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites multi-year AI data-centre and smart-manufacturing contracts, expansion into European infrastructure and energy transition, and new customer wins.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk of deceleration in US construction capex after midterms?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says data-centre contracts are multi-year with capital committed upfront and cancellations are unlikely; it sees no slowdown in order books and no change in delivery schedules.

qa_highlights.question: What is the M&A strategy and cash deployment plan?
qa_highlights.answer: About half a dozen acquisition opportunities are under evaluation, mainly in hydraulics/PTO in Europe and large fabrication in India; two deals were walked away from recently. Acquisitions are the first use of cash, otherwise the board will decide on distribution.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise, and what drives FY28 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher freight cost drove other expenses; to be passed to customers. Growth drivers are construction, small ag recovery, large ag new wins and fabrication (12-15% of new wins).

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital and inventory rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables rose with higher revenue and delays from one or two US customers, one resolved and one expected to resolve in November; management says these are not disputes. Working capital is at 137 days, expected to stay 136-140 days.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 be better than H1 and what about Mexico?
qa_highlights.answer: H2 FY27 growth will be lower than H1 because of the high H2 FY26 base; Q3 will be seasonally weaker but above Q1. Mexico revenue started in November, with no Q2 contribution.

risks_watch: Farm (large ag) volume decline of about 17% industry-wide, with recovery not yet visible at industry level.
Concentration and payment timing with one or two US customers driving receivables and working capital (137 days).
Steel and commodity cost pass-through lag that may pressure margins until price increases are recovered.
Possible US regulatory scrutiny (FTC/USDA inquiry into ag equipment makers), though management sees no impact.
Execution of fabrication and Mexico ramp-up; acquisition pipeline and capital deployment decisions.
Other expenses (freight) elevated in Q2; recovery expected next quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident on construction and margins, with specific numbers on growth and order wins; cautious on H2 and Q3 seasonality. Management was measured and somewhat evasive on Europe demand and on how acquisition cash would be deployed, giving no timeline.

growth.why: Management reiterates FY27 revenue about 24% above FY26 with H2 growth of about 10%, backed by ₹225 crore trailing new business wins, a construction order book and the Mexico facility, though no hard capacity numbers were given beyond ~₹60 crore capex over the next year.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin 23.4% vs 20% through-cycle target, material cost 34.3% with some steel inflation not yet passed through, and freight cost expected to be recovered next quarter; offset by H2 seasonality and high-base growth slowing to ~10%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Mexico facility began first customer dispatches in November 2026 with single-digit USD million revenue expected in next six months, and fabrication expansion at the India facility is under construction; no hard capacity numbers given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management reiterates FY27 revenue ~24% above FY26 with H2 growth ~10%, backed by ₹225 crore trailing new business wins and construction sales up 49% YoY, though large ag industry volumes are down ~17%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: About ₹60 crore capex is planned over the next year, mostly already approved with advances paid, so new project announcements are plausible but the existing plan is largely committed; utilisation not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth guidance of ~24% was reiterated (described as raised in the brief), with H1 revenue up 32%, but H2 growth is guided down to ~10% on the high H2 FY26 base, limiting upside.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q3 is guided seasonally weaker, large ag volumes are down ~17% industry-wide, and receivable delays with one or two US customers and steel pass-through lag could pressure H2 numbers.

rows.label: Mexico facility ramp-up
rows.why: First customer dispatches began Nov 2026; single-digit USD million revenue expected in next six months with three customers in discussion.

rows.label: Acquisitions as first use of cash
rows.why: About half a dozen opportunities under evaluation (hydraulics/PTO in Europe, large fabrication in India); two deals walked away from, and no timeline was given; dividends are the fallback if no deal.

rows.label: Fabrication scale-up
rows.why: Fabrication is 12-15% of new business wins and management targets high single-digit % of revenue from under 2% today, with capability expansion underway.

tone.note: Management was confident on construction growth, margins and the 24% FY27 revenue outlook, but cautious on H2 seasonality and high-base slowdown; analysts pushed on Europe demand, steel pass-through, receivables and acquisition cash deployment, where answers were less specific.
